title: Visa's AI Shopping Test: 22 Models Fail 43% of Purchases
dek: Visa's new benchmark shows AI agents still buy the wrong thing for you.

facts.label: Overall pass rate across 22 AI models
Failed runs that still made a purchase

caption:
Would you let an AI spend your money? Visa just tested 22 of them, and they failed 42.8% of shopping tasks. 🛒

The new Visa Agentic Commerce Benchmark puts AI agents in realistic conversations with shoppers looking for TVs, laptops and personal care appliances. To pass, a model has to uncover every hidden need, like budget or HDR10+ support, and then make the right call to buy or not buy. The best model passed 82.2% of runs, the worst just 28.9%.

The scariest part: about 54% of failed runs still ended with the AI buying something. Consistency was weak too. All three attempts at the same task passed only about a third of the time.

Here at AI Parabellum, our takeaway for agentic commerce is simple. Use AI shopping agents for research, give them your budget and must-haves up front, and always check the final pick before you pay.

post_caption:
Pricier AI models shopped better, but price didn't guarantee success. In Visa's new benchmark, the five most expensive models passed 67.1% of runs versus 50.2% for the cheapest.

The gap matters because only 23% of US consumers trust AI to handle payments. Visa plans to add checkout and payment testing next. Let AI help you research, but keep the final say. 💳
